cards.text: For chapters now, the writer of Chronicles has been listing family after family (1 Chronicles 1-8), and here he wraps it up: all Israel was recorded in the genealogies written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. Then comes the hard news. Judah was exiled to Babylon.

cards.question: The writer tells us why. Judah was exiled to Babylon because of their ___.

cards.text: But the story doesn't end in Babylon. People are moving back onto their own property in their cities, and somebody has to be first through the door.

cards.question: Who are among the first to resettle their own property in their cities?

cards.text: Some of the people of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh settle in Jerusalem itself. Then comes the roll call: families from Judah and Benjamin, then the priests, then the Levites. The Benjamites come with 956 relatives, and the priests with 1,760, all able men for the work of the service of the house of God.

Next come the gatekeepers, with Shallum as their chief, guarding the thresholds of the Tent just like their fathers before them. Way back, Phinehas son of Eleazar was in charge of the gatekeepers, and the LORD was with him. And Zechariah son of Meshelemiah keeps the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, and I would have PAID for a gatekeeper deciding what got tossed in on top of me.
All told, 212 men are chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds, registered by genealogy in their villages. And these aren't jobs you grab off a sign-up sheet by the break room, friend.

cards.question: David, Israel's king, and Samuel the seer had appointed the gatekeepers to their positions of ___.

cards.text: So the gatekeepers and their descendants guard the gates of the house of the LORD, the house called the Tent, stationed on all four sides. Their relatives come in from the villages at fixed times to serve with them for seven days at a time, and the four chief gatekeepers, who are Levites, are trusted with the rooms and the treasuries. Generations of door duty, so that family reunion has the BEST security in town.
Night falls, and those four chief gatekeepers don't clock out. They spend the night stationed all around the house of God.

cards.question: Why do the four chief gatekeepers spend the night around the house of God?

answers.text: They guard it and open it each morning
They have no homes of their own
They are fasting for the feast

cards.text: Some of these men are put in charge of the articles used in worship.

cards.question: True or false: the men in charge of the articles used in worship count them whenever they're brought in or taken out.

cards.text: Others look after the sanctuary's furnishings, plus the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense and spices, and some of the priests' sons mix the spices. A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, is trusted with baking the bread, and some Kohathites, a Levite clan, prepare the rows of the showbread every Sabbath. Baking the bread? My mustache just stood straight up, friend. That's MY side of the kitchen!
Then there are the musicians, heads of Levite families who stay in the temple chambers. And they're excused from other duties.

cards.question: Why are the musicians exempt from other duties?

answers.text: They are on duty day and night
Their families serve in their place

cards.text: All these heads of Levite families live in Jerusalem. Then the writer lists one more family, the family of Jeiel the father of Gibeon, and a big name shows up: Kish was the father of Saul, the man the people made king of Israel (1 Samuel 11:15). From Saul's son Jonathan, the line runs all the way down to Azel and his six sons.
